questions.question:
The inverse Laplace transform of the function [latex]F(s)=\frac{1}{s(s+1)}[/latex]
 is given by
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} &\begin{aligned} F(s) &=\frac{1}{s(s+1)}=\frac{A}{s}+\frac{B}{s+1} \\ &=\frac{A(s+1)+B(s)}{s(s+1)} \end{aligned}\\ &\Rightarrow A(s+1)+B(s)=0\\ &\text { Put } \quad s=0\\ &\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow & A=1 \\ \text { and } & s=-1 \end{array}\\ &\Rightarrow \quad B=-1\\ &\text { So } \quad F(s)=\frac{1}{s}-\frac{1}{s+1}\\ &\begin{aligned} \text { Now } & f(t)=L^{-1}(F(s))=e^{0 t}-e^{-t} \\ & f(t)=1-e^{-t} \end{aligned} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question:
An ideal gas of mass m and temperature [latex]T_{1}[/latex]
 undergoes a reversible isothermal process from an initial pressure [latex]P_{1}[/latex]
 to final pressure [latex]P_{2}[/latex]
 . The heat loss using the process is Q. the entropy change [latex]\Delta[/latex]S of the gas is
questions.explanation: We know that [latex] \Delta S=\frac{\delta Q}{T}[/latex] Integrating between states 1 and 2 gives [latex] \begin{aligned} \int_{1}^{2} \Delta S &=\int_{1}^{2} \frac{\delta Q}{T} \\ S_{2}-S_{1} &=\frac{1}{T} \int_{1}^{2} \delta Q \quad \because T=C\\ &=\frac{1}{T} \times Q_{1-2}=\frac{m R T \ln \frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}}{T} \\ &=m R \ln \frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}=m R \ln \frac{P_{1}}{P_{2}} \end{aligned}[/latex] where [latex]\frac{P_{1}}{P_{2}}=\frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}[/latex] for isothermal process Alternatively We know that the entropy change in terms of temperature and pressure ratios, [latex] S_{2}-S_{1}=m c_{P} \ln \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}-m R \ln \frac{P_{2}}{P_{1}}[/latex] where [latex] T_{1}=T_{2} [/latex] for isothermal process [latex] \therefore \quad S_{2}-S_{1}=-m R \ln \frac{P_{2}}{P_{1}}=m R \ln \frac{P_{1}}{P_{2}}[/latex]

We know that
[latex] \Delta S=\frac{\delta Q}{T}[/latex]

[latex] \begin{aligned} \int_{1}^{2} \Delta S &=\int_{1}^{2} \frac{\delta Q}{T} \\ S_{2}-S_{1} &=\frac{1}{T} \int_{1}^{2} \delta Q \quad \because T=C\\ &=\frac{1}{T} \times Q_{1-2}=\frac{m R T \ln \frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}}{T} \\ &=m R \ln \frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}=m R \ln \frac{P_{1}}{P_{2}} \end{aligned}[/latex]
where [latex]\frac{P_{1}}{P_{2}}=\frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}[/latex] for isothermal process
Alternatively
We know that the entropy change in terms of temperature and pressure ratios,

where [latex] T_{1}=T_{2} [/latex] for isothermal process
